title: The Two Balconies of Sana'a
subtitle: A storyworld where love meets inherited grievance
about: Romeo and Juliet set in Sana'a between a Sunni boy and a Shia girl. Rami al-Hakimi, a calligrapher's son, and Zahra al-Mutawakkil, a doctor's daughter, fall in love while their families, neighborhood councils, checkpoints, clerics, and friends make every private choice public.

characters.name: Rami al-Hakimi
characters.role: Sunni boy, apprentice calligrapher, impulsive but morally serious

characters.name: Zahra al-Mutawakkil
characters.role: Shia girl, medical student, sharp observer, unwilling to be reduced to symbol

characters.name: Layla
characters.role: Zahra's cousin, practical mediator with divided loyalties

characters.name: Yasin
characters.role: Rami's friend, poet and rumor-runner who can inflame or repair

variables.name: Secrecy_Disclosure
variables.description: whether love, violence, and bargains stay hidden or become accountable

variables.name: Family_Truce
variables.description: whether family honor hardens into feud or opens toward negotiated truce

variables.name: Sectarian_Trust
variables.description: whether religious identity becomes threat, bridge, or shared vocabulary

variables.name: Love_Duty
variables.description: whether private love escapes duty, transforms it, or is crushed by it

encounters.title: First Glimpse at the Friday Market
encounters.description: Rami carries ink jars through the old souq. A woman in navy headscarf pauses before his father's calligraphy shop, tracing letters with her eye.

options.text: Watch from behind the doorframe
Step forward and greet her
Lower your head and pass by quickly

encounters.title: The Name on the Street
encounters.description: She turns. You see her clearly now. A neighbor passes, slows slightly, looks between you both. The air tightens.

options.text: Ask: What do you seek at this shop?
Say nothing. Let silence bridge the distance.
Turn away before anyone can speak of this.

encounters.title: A Shared Verse at the Copyist's Stall
encounters.description: Days later, you find her at a copyist's stall in Bab al-Yemen. She holds a small book of pre-Islamic poetry. Her finger rests on a line about two stars that cannot meet.

options.text: Recite the next verse with her
Ask who gave her this book
Step back. This is not your place.

encounters.title: The Boundary Line on Bab al-Yemen
encounters.description: Yasin approaches, grinning. He says he's heard someone speak of the al-Hakimi boy and an al-Mutawakkil girl meeting at the copyist's stall. His eyes dance.

options.text: Tell him nothing happened
Ask how he heard anything of it
Challenge him: Who else has spoken?

secret_option.text: Ask what Yasin plans to do with the story
secret_option.unlock_condition: Player has chosen a 'witness' or 'transmission' option previously

encounters.title: The Father's Warning
encounters.description: Your father calls you to the shop. He does not look at you as he speaks of how the al-Mutawakkil family has never trusted them, and how trust, once broken, takes generations to mend.

options.text: Listen and say nothing
Ask what broke the trust between families
Say: I do not carry their grievance

encounters.title: Layla at the Well in Bab al-Sha'b
encounters.description: You meet Zahra's cousin Layla by accident near the old well. She knows you from school. She speaks of how her cousin is being watched, how girls from their family must be careful.

options.text: Ask if she will help convey a message
Tell her you mean no harm to anyone
Leave before she sees too much of your face

encounters.title: The Checkpoint at Night
encounters.description: You pass a neighborhood checkpoint late. The guards exchange glances as your name is called out. Someone recognizes you.

options.text: Give your name and wait
Claim you are visiting a sick friend
Ask what they want from you

encounters.title: First Choice: Meet or Retreat?
encounters.description: The pattern is clear now. Eyes follow you. Names are mentioned in passing. A note has been passed to Zahra through Layla, asking for one meeting at the old fountain behind Al-Azhar Mosque.

options.text: Go to the fountain alone
Send Yasin to ask if Layla can meet instead
Write back that this must wait until the families are ready

encounters.title: The Vertical Meeting
encounters.theme: The balcony scene reimagined through Sana'a's stacked houses and connecting stairs
encounters.body: Rami climbs the narrow external stairway during tarawih prayers, reaching Zahra's wooden balcony overlooking the walled courtyard. She appears wrapped in a light scarf, smelling of eucalyptus oil from her clinic shift. They speak through the lattice screen—her hand brushing his as she hands him a pressed jasmine flower from the garden below.

options.text: Recite poetry that bridges their sects
Exchange personal tokens secretly beneath the screen
Promise to meet again under cover of night

encounters.title: The Clinic Window
encounters.theme: Rami witnesses Zahra's competence and compassion at her hospital rotation
encounters.body: Delivering calligraphy for the hospital entrance, Rami hides behind a curtain as he watches Zahra tend to an injured boy from his own neighborhood. She speaks gentle words in Arabic, bandaging wounds with skilled hands. When she catches his eye through the window glass, she does not flee—she offers him a small nod of recognition.

options.text: Approach her and thank her for caring for your people
Leave a piece of calligraphy anonymously on her desk
Flee before anyone sees you together

encounters.title: The Wedding Rumor
encounters.theme: Yasin brings news that Zahra is being betrothed to a cousin from Najaf
encounters.body: At the coffee house, Yasin leans close with urgent whisper. The Mutawakkil family has announced an engagement—Zahra will marry a nephew of the Imam in Iraq, a union meant to strengthen sectarian ties. Rami's pen freezes mid-stroke over his parchment. Three months. That is when the wedding feast begins.

options.text: Confront the elders directly about this arrangement
Send a message through Layla asking for her truth
Accept this as fate and withdraw your heart

secret_option.text: Reveal yourself to Zahra publicly, risking everything on love

encounters.title: The Hakimi Council
encounters.theme: Rami's father speaks with the family about his future and a proposed marriage alliance
encounters.body: Rami's father sits him down among uncles in the qubbah, speaking of duty. A daughter from the al-Imadi family has been proposed—a Sunni bride from a respected lineage. Rami watches ink dry on calligraphy sheets while elders discuss his future as if he were property to be traded for alliance and honor.

options.text: Cite Islamic tradition that requires consent in marriage
Declare your intention to study further abroad first
Ask for time to pray on the matter

encounters.title: The Street Confrontation
encounters.theme: First violent escalation when families encounter in public space
encounters.body: At the Friday market, a Hakimi merchant and Mutawakkil vendor trade words that escalate quickly. Stones fly. Rami watches Zahra being pushed back by her family into their doorway. He steps forward to help—his father's hand clamps on his shoulder, dragging him backward as neighbors form a watching circle.

options.text: Let your father take you away before violence spreads
Attempt to separate the families with peaceful words
Throw down your calligraphy tools in protest

encounters.title: The Elder's Warning
encounters.theme: A neutral elder warns Rami about the consequences of cross-sect love
encounters.body: Sheikh Abdullah, respected by both families, calls Rami into his study after prayers. The old man speaks plainly: he knows. He has seen the glances exchanged during Ramadan gatherings. Such unions bring not just heartbreak but bloodshed. Sana'a is narrow—there is nowhere for forbidden love to hide.

options.text: Ask what wisdom exists beyond fear and tradition
Request he write a letter of introduction to Zahra's family
Plead with him to mediate between the families

encounters.title: The Marketplace Declaration
encounters.theme: Rami publicly declares his love, forcing a crisis
encounters.body: During the midday call to prayer at the old mosque square, Rami stands on the fountain's edge. He calls Zahra's name aloud—his voice carrying over the marketplace silence as men turn from their prayers. Her family appears in the doorway, faces hard with fury and shame.

options.text: Continue speaking until she steps forward to you
Beg for forgiveness before descending into chaos
Recite verses about love that transcends division

secret_option.text: Call out her name and demand she choose you openly

encounters.title: The Night Flight Plan
encounters.theme: Layla offers a dangerous escape route through the city's hidden passages
encounters.body: Layla meets Rami in the abandoned madrasa courtyard. She has heard everything from her cousin—Zahra will not consent to the arranged marriage, nor can she openly defy her family. Layla knows the old water channels beneath Sana'a that lead out toward the desert roads. But once you leave, there is no return.

options.text: Agree to flee together with Zahra at dawn
Refuse and instead fight for recognition through proper channels
Ask Layla to deliver one final message before you decide

encounters.title: The Olive Grove Pact
encounters.summary: Beneath the ancient olive trees outside Sana'a, Rami and Zahra seal their secret vow.
encounters.text:
The moon hangs low over the olive grove. Zahra's hand trembles slightly as she holds out a small object—a silver ring, her grandmother's, passed down through generations of women who navigated impossible choices.

'I won't ask you to abandon your family,' Zahra says quietly. 'But I need to know that when they call for you to march, to protest, to hate—I'll be worth the cost.'

Rami looks at her, then at the ring. The city lights of Sana'a glow in the distance.

'What do I say?' Rami asks.

options.text: "I choose you. Whatever comes after is theirs to bear, not me."
options.outcome: Rami commits fully. Love_Duty shifts toward love (+20). Secrecy_Disclosure rises slightly as passion clouds caution.

options.text: "Let me find a way to bring our families together first."
options.outcome: Rami seeks balance, but Zahra sees hesitation. Family_Truce gains ground while Love_Duty stays contested.

options.text: "I'm yours, but I can't promise what the future holds."
options.outcome: An honest answer that wounds Zahra's certainty. She accepts it but marks him as uncertain.

encounters.title: The Clinic Warning
encounters.summary: Dr. Al-Haddad, who treats both Sunni and Shia patients, pulls Rami aside after hours.
encounters.text:
Dr. Al-Haddad is a man who has seen too many young people arrive at his clinic with wounds that weren't meant for them. He pours two glasses of tea in the quiet clinic.

'I'm not here to lecture,' he says. 'But your father came through my doors yesterday—Sunni anger makes him reckless, and I saw it in his eyes. When men like him get cornered by pride, they don't think about consequences.'

He sets down his glass.

'If Zahra's family learns of you before the truce is real, Rami—you'll be an excuse for violence on both sides. Not a cause of love.'

options.text: "Then tell me how to make that truce happen."
options.outcome: The doctor offers cautious advice about approaching the elders through respected intermediaries.

options.text: "I'll be careful. We both will."
options.outcome: The doctor nods but his expression suggests he's heard this before from others who weren't careful enough.

options.text: "What would you have me do? End it now?"
options.outcome: The doctor shakes his head slowly. 'I didn't say that. I said be wise.' A non-answer, but honest.

encounters.title: The Checkpoint at Bab al-Yemen
encounters.summary: Zahra must cross a neighborhood checkpoint to reach the meeting place.
encounters.text:
Bab al-Yemen is more than an entrance—it's a statement. Tonight, young men in dark shirts stand near the archway, not official but never challenged by those who are.

One of them—Zahra recognizes him from her uncle's circle—calls out as she approaches with her bag.

'Late for something?' He smirks. 'Or someone?'

Behind him, his friends watch. Her phone is dead; she can't call Rami to cancel without explanation.

options.text: "Going to the clinic. Dr. Al-Haddad needs me for hours." (Lie with plausible cover)
options.outcome: The boy considers it, then waves her through. Secrecy_Disclosure drops slightly—she navigated well.

options.text: "What would you have me say?" (Defiant, risky)
options.outcome: He lets her pass but mutters something to his friend that makes Zahra's stomach turn. She'll hear about this.

options.text: "My aunt is ill. Let me pass." (Appeal to family duty)
options.outcome: He grins, respects the excuse even as he mocks it. 'Tell her I said get well.' Passes without incident.

encounters.title: Yasin's Mistake
encounters.summary: Yasin tries to help by delivering a message but nearly compromises them.
encounters.text:
Yasin burst into Rami's room, breathless with pride. 'I found her cousin—Nadia, the one studying engineering in Cairo during summer break. She's coming back next week, I told her you wanted to discuss... community service projects.'

Rami freezes. Zahra has no cousin named Nadia.

'Yasin,' Rami says carefully. 'What did you tell her exactly?'

options.text: "Start from the beginning and don't leave anything out." (Confront)
options.outcome: Yasin's face falls as he realizes his mistake. Damage control begins immediately.

options.text: "Who else knows you're involved in this?" (Damage assessment)
options.outcome: Yasin counts on his fingers. Three people at minimum, all of whom think it's a 'noble cause.'

options.text: "I'll handle it. You just... don't say anything more." (Shut him down)
options.outcome: Yasin nods solemnly, but Rami knows better. The enthusiasm is already spent.

secret_option.condition: If player has demonstrated cleverness in previous encounters (Love_Duty > 40 AND Secrecy_Disclosure < 30)
secret_option.text: "Nadia's coming back? Tell her I need her help with something else. Something she shouldn't write down." (Redirect)
secret_option.outcome: Rami spins Yasin's mistake into a cover story that gives him breathing room to fix the real problem.

encounters.title: The Family Council
encounters.summary: Rami's father calls a gathering of family elders—something is brewing.
encounters.text:
The room smells of qat and old paper. Rami sits on the edge of his cushion as his uncles speak in low tones.

'You know what they're saying about the clinic,' his uncle says, not looking at him. 'That our boys are being soft, that we've forgotten what it means to protect our own.'

His father speaks next, voice grave. 'There's a gathering planned for Friday. A statement. We need every son who still has honor in his blood.'

options.text: "I'll be there." (Commit—dangerous path)
options.outcome: His father nods, satisfied. But Rami now carries the weight of a promise that puts him directly against Zahra's family.

options.text: "I have university. Can't miss the semester." (Excuse)
options.outcome: His uncle scoffs but his father only says, 'We'll see.' The doubt is planted.

options.text: "What statement do you want made?" (Seek clarity)
options.outcome: His father's answer is vague: 'The kind that makes people remember who they are.' Rami doesn't sleep well.

encounters.title: Cousins at the Market
encounters.summary: Taher, Rami's cousin, runs into Zahra's brother at the spice market.
encounters.text:
The spice market is crowded with morning shoppers. Taher—boisterous, proud, the kind of man who wears his Sunni identity like armor—blocks the aisle.

'Well, if it isn't Abdullah,' Taher says loudly enough for neighbors to hear. 'Come praying we forget your people's sins?' 

Abdullah doesn't rise to it initially. But then Taher pushes past him, shoulder checking hard enough to knock a woman's basket over.

Spices scatter across the stone floor.

options.text: "Rami intervenes if present—pulls Taher back." (If Rami is there)
options.outcome: Taher scoffs at his cousin but backs down. Abdullah thanks him quietly, eyes cold.

options.text: "Abdullah lets it go—focuses on helping the woman." (If Rami absent)
options.outcome: Taher mutters something about 'softness' but the crowd's disapproval makes him leave.

options.text: "Abdullah responds in kind—words for words." (Escalation)
options.outcome: The exchange grows heated. A shopkeeper separates them before hands come out.

encounters.title: The Public Square Gathering
encounters.summary: Friday prayers draw crowds to the square—tensions are high.
encounters.text:
The square fills with men after prayer. Voices rise in recitation, then in speech. Someone brings a speaker.

Rami stands at the edge of the crowd, Zahra somewhere out there too—he knows she would come despite everything. The speaker's voice amplifies: 'They say we should forget! But forgetting is how they take us!' 

A stone flies—no one claims it—and hits a young man from the other neighborhood in the shoulder.

The square goes still, then erupts.

options.text: "Push through to Zahra's side of the square." (Find her)
options.outcome: Rami finds her briefly—they exchange a look of pure terror—before the crowd separates them violently.

options.text: "Get out before it gets worse." (Flee)
options.outcome: Rami slips away while the crowd's attention is on the wounded man. He missed her, but he's alive.

options.text: "Stay and help whoever needs it." (Humanity first)
options.outcome: Rami helps carry the wounded man to a clinic. Dr. Al-Haddad sees him, doesn't comment.

encounters.title: Blood in the Alley
encounters.summary: A confrontation after the square incident leaves someone seriously wounded.
encounters.text:
The alley behind the market is dark and narrow. Taher cornered—three men, all from neighborhoods that don't forgive.

They didn't want to kill him. Just teach him a lesson about 'respect.'

Rami arrives too late to prevent it but in time to see his cousin slumped against the wall, blood soaking through his shirt, one of the attackers still standing over him.

Taher looks up, sees Rami.

'Run,' Taher whispers. 'Don't be stupid.'

options.text: "Stay and help my cousin." (Duty)
options.outcome: Rami carries Taher to the clinic. His father finds out—knows now that Rami was there, in the wrong place at the wrong time.

options.text: "Call an ambulance and run." (Pragmatic)
options.outcome: Taher survives but wakes to find his cousin vanished. The family will hunt for him.

options.text: "Confront the attacker." (Dangerous)
options.outcome: Rami drives him off but takes a wound himself. Now both cousins are wounded, and Zahra's people are involved.

encounters.title: The Exile Threat
encounters.description: Abdullah has summoned Rami to the family compound. News travels fast in Sana'a, and your father says he can no longer protect you here if you continue this path.
encounters.text: "You have shamed us," Abdullah says from behind his desk. "A Shia girl. In public. With half the market watching." He slides a paper across the mahogany. "My brother's family has arrangements in Dammam. You will leave tomorrow."

options.label: [procedure] Request time to finish exams before leaving
[justice] Demand to know what punishment Zahra faces
[disclosure] Reveal you've already told her family about us

encounters.title: Family Ultimatum
encounters.description: You've stalled the exile, but Abdullah has brought in reinforcements. A cousin from Riyadh is here to discuss 'arrangements' for both your future.
encounters.text: The air in the room grows heavy with the presence of Uncle Mahmoud from Riyadh. He brings news of a suitable bride—daughter of a prominent family in Jeddah, well-educated, understanding. "You're twenty," he says. "It's time to think like a man, not a boy dreaming fantasies."

options.label: [order] Agree to meet the woman, buy more time
[identity] Reject outright—say you've already chosen
[symbol] Show them Zahra's clinic volunteer certificate—she helps everyone

encounters.title: Zahra's Clinic Plan
encounters.description: You slip away to the clinic where Zahra works. She's heard rumors and has a plan of her own.
encounters.text: "My uncle wants to use us as leverage," Zahra says, voice low behind the pharmacy counter. "But my mother—she doesn't want war." She shows you papers: transfer records for a student exchange program in Beirut. Two universities with partnerships. "We study together there. The distance makes us forget nothing, but makes everything survivable."

options.label: [transmission] Agree—send the application tomorrow
[community] Suggest involving respected teachers as intermediaries first
[mercy] Tell her you can't leave your family like this—they need me

encounters.title: Rami's Hiding Place
encounters.description: The pressure is too much. You need somewhere to think, somewhere the city can't find you.
encounters.text: You find yourself at the old Ottoman-era house your grandfather once owned—now abandoned, keys hidden under a loose stone in the courtyard wall. Inside, time has stood still. Your grandmother's calligraphy hangs on one wall. A place where she taught you to read before she died, before the divide hardened between Sunni and Shia neighbors.

options.label: [spirit] Pray here, ask for clarity
[letter] Write to Zahra—tell her everything you've been afraid to say
[purpose] Make a decision: you won't let them break this

secret_option.label: [witness] Find your grandmother's old notebook—she wrote about her own forbidden love

encounters.title: The False Death Rumor
encounters.description: Morning brings news that stops the city in its tracks.
encounters.text: By dawn, whispers have become certainty: Zahra is dead. A car accident on the way to university. The rumor spreads faster than truth—through mosque announcements, WhatsApp groups, market gossip. You find yourself outside her family's house as men arrive with condolences.

options.label: [reason] Knock and ask directly before believing
[transmission] Call her phone—she won't answer if she's gone
[veil] Let it pass—some truths aren't yours to confirm yet

encounters.title: The Living Truth
encounters.description: You find Zahra at the clinic, bruised and angry.
encounters.text: "Someone wanted our families to stop negotiating," she says, pressing ice to a cut on her temple. "Uncle Hassan's friends spread it. If my family thinks you're grieving, they'll push for blood money or revenge—and that locks us into being enemies forever." She looks at you with something harder than love now.

options.label: [consensus] Go together to both families—end the rumors publicly
[mercy] Leave her be—she needs to handle her own family
[justice] Confront Hassan directly—he started this

encounters.title: Elders as Witnesses
encounters.description: You've gathered a small group—two Sunni elders, two Shia. They sit in a quiet teahouse on the edge of the old city.
encounters.text: "We're not here to bless anything," says Sheikh Omar, Sunni elder and respected teacher. "But if tragedy is coming, I want it known that we tried otherwise." Zahra's uncle Hassan arrives late, scowling. The city has heard you plan to meet—someone will be watching.

options.label: [precedent] Share the story of your grandmother and her lost love
[community] Ask them to mediate a formal truce between families
[order] Propose the Beirut plan formally—let them decide

secret_option.label: [witness] Present evidence that Hassan orchestrated the death rumor
secret_option.requirement: has item 'clinic security footage' or Sectarian_Trust <= -1

encounters.title: The City Watches
encounters.description: The meeting breaks up as shouts echo from the street. Someone has brought your families here.
encounters.text: Abdullah stands at the teahouse entrance, face unreadable. Behind him, Amina holds Zahra's hand tightly. The elders rise uncertainly. Sheikh Omar speaks first: "You've come for answers. But the question is whether you're ready to hear what repair actually costs." The street fills with onlookers.

options.label: [disclosure] Step forward and take Zahra's hand—let the city see
[mercy] Let your father speak first—give him dignity
[symbol] Offer the Beirut papers as a third path

encounters.title: The Last Messenger
encounters.description: You seek Shaykh Ibrahim, an elder known to counsel both families. He agrees to hear your plea—but warns you the feud runs deeper than one conversation.
encounters.text: Shaykh Ibrahim listens in silence as you explain. When you finish, he sighs, removing his glasses. 'The Al-Zahrani and Al-Husayni families have been enemies since before either of you was born,' he says. 'Your grandfather killed my cousin's brother-in-law over a land dispute mixed with sectarian rhetoric. The wound has festered through three generations.' He pauses. 'I can try—but I cannot promise the men will listen to reason when fear and reputation speak louder.'

options.text: Ask him to meet with both fathers together, presenting your case directly
Request he speak to each father separately first, then bring them together
Accept his warning and prepare for another path entirely

encounters.title: Night Refuge in the Old Quarter
encounters.description: The shaykh's attempt fails—each father refuses even to enter the same room. You and Layla seek refuge in an abandoned courtyard house in the old quarter, where a sympathetic midwife lets you stay.
encounters.text: Midnight. The courtyard is quiet except for distant prayer calls blending from Sunni and Shia mosques nearby. Layla sits beside you on the stone floor, her head on your shoulder. 'We cannot stay hidden forever,' she whispers. 'The midwife cannot protect us indefinitely.' You look at each other—lovers who have found no shelter in this city of divided loyalties.

options.text: Plan to flee Sana'a together while the night still offers cover
Stay hidden longer—hope may yet find a way through
Make a public statement tomorrow—force the city to witness your love

secret_option.text: [Hidden] Speak with the midwife about gathering witnesses to the feud's machinery
secret_option.requirement: Sectarian_Trust >= 40 AND player has chosen 'community' or 'consensus' in previous encounters

encounters.title: The Disappearance
encounters.description: Days pass. Rumors spread through Sana'a's markets and mosques—whispers that Layla has vanished, or worse.
encounters.text: Your mother finds you at the university: 'They say she collapsed in hiding and died alone.' But you know Layla better than death knows her heart. You search the old quarter, the clinic where she sometimes volunteers, the mosque courtyard where you first kissed. Nothing. Then a letter arrives—not from her hand, but sealed with Al-Husayni insignia: 'She has been taken to Taiz by relatives for her safety.'

options.text: Ride to Taiz immediately—nothing will stop you from reaching her
Wait and send a message through the midwife first
Confront your father—demand he help you find her before it's too late

encounters.title: The Gathering at Al-Sumayya Mosque
encounters.description: A community gathering is called—not for prayer, but to address the growing scandal. Both families are present. The city watches.
encounters.text: Al-Sumayya mosque courtyard fills with men and women from both quarters. Your father stands beside Omar Al-Husayni—Layla's uncle—who holds a letter in his hand. 'We have received word,' he announces, 'that the young woman is alive, but has fled Sana'a with her lover.' Silence falls. Eyes turn toward you. The city demands an account.

options.text: Step forward and admit everything—take full responsibility
Remain silent—let the elders speak first
Speak of love transcending division—appeal to the community's better nature

encounters.title: The Choice Before the Verdict
encounters.description: The elders reach a preliminary consensus. You have one moment to speak before the final judgment is delivered.
encounters.text: Shaykh Ibrahim turns to you: 'The community must decide your fate, young man. Will you be exiled for dishonoring both families? Will you be forced into marriage with another woman to repair the Al-Zahrani name? Or will some other path be found?' He looks at your father, then at Omar Al-Husayni. The men exchange glances—calculations of reputation, fear, and something softer that might be regret.

options.text: Accept exile—leave Sana'a to preserve family honor while staying with Layla
Demand the right to marry Layla properly—through all due channels
Offer yourself to community service—work for reconciliation as penance

secret_option.text: [Hidden] Call for the community itself to testify about how it produced this tragedy
secret_option.requirement: unlock_secret_bridge is true OR player has chosen 'witness' or 'disclosure' three times

encounters.title: The City's Judgment
encounters.description: The verdict approaches. Families, clerics, and neighbors gather for the final decision that will determine your future.
encounters.text: Sunset paints Sana'a in gold and crimson. The courtyard has become a courtroom of tradition and fear. Your father's face shows conflict—pride warring with something like love. Omar Al-Husayni clears his throat: 'The girl is found to be alive, hiding in Taiz. She has sent word she will not return without him.' He looks at you. 'We have three options before us. And the city waits for our wisdom—or our judgment.'

options.text: Accept whatever verdict comes—trust that justice and mercy will balance
Appeal to higher authorities—the governor, the university board
Propose a truce ceremony—publicly declare both families' commitment to peace

final_encounter: The courtyard falls silent as the elders deliver their verdict. Your father looks at you with eyes that hold both anger and grief. Omar Al-Husayni speaks first: 'We will not kill our children for loving.' Then your father: 'But we cannot let love destroy honor.' The compromise emerges—exile, marriage elsewhere, a fragile peace between families bought with your absence from the city that made you.
secret_bridge: You stand before the gathered crowd and speak not of your own fate, but of theirs. 'Who taught us to hate?' you ask. 'Which checkpoint man first stopped Shia children from playing in Sunni streets? Which cleric first called our brothers heretics? Which merchant first refused trade on sectarian grounds?' One by one, men step forward—clerics admitting fear drove their rhetoric, checkpoint guards confessing they enforced division for power, neighbors revealing how rumors were manufactured. The tragedy becomes collective testimony.

endings.title: Administrative Truce
endings.text: The governor intervenes with bureaucratic efficiency. A memorandum is signed: the Al-Zahrani and Al-Husayni families shall cease hostilities under penalty of fines. You and Layla are permitted to marry, provided you register your union within thirty days and relocate outside Sana'a's city limits. Love survives, administered by state machinery that neither understands nor cares about hearts.

endings.title: Family Victory
endings.text: Honor prevails. Your father arranges your marriage to the daughter of a respected Sunni family in Aden. Layla is wed to her cousin in Beirut, far from Sana'a's divided streets. Years later, you hear rumors—she writes poetry about a boy she loved once; you keep a green scarf tucked inside your Quran. Both families celebrate their victory over love.

endings.title: Exile Together
endings.text: You flee Sana'a under cover of night, heading north toward Aleppo where neither family's reach extends. In a small apartment overlooking the Syrian coast, you build a life—no grand ceremonies, no community blessing, just two hearts that found each other against impossible odds. Sometimes you pray for home, but home is wherever Layla sleeps beside you.

endings.title: The Tragedy
endings.text: Desperate and cornered, you seek each other one final night in the abandoned house where you first made love. A vial of medicine—meant for your mother's pain—is mislabeled, misunderstood. You drink together, promising to meet wherever death leads. When your families find you, they hold each other's hands across the bodies of children who died believing love could conquer division.

endings.title: Clinic Reconciliation
endings.text: You propose working together at a neutral clinic on the border between Sunni and Shia quarters. For six months, you treat patients side by side—Sunni mothers, Shia fathers, all bleeding the same red blood. Your fathers watch from afar as their children heal strangers without asking sect or family. Eventually, they approach each other—not as enemies, but as parents who finally understand.

endings.title: Poetic Legend
endings.text: Your story becomes Sana'a's own Romeo and Juliet—sung by mothers to restless daughters, quoted by lovers who believe theirs is the first great love. A poet writes a qasida about Karim and Layla that spreads through Yemen and beyond. Your families eventually reconcile, not for your sakes but because your legend brought shame to their feud. You are dead to them, yet alive in poetry forever.

endings.title: Fragile Council
endings.text: Your trial becomes the catalyst for something larger. Sunni and Shia elders form a reconciliation council, meeting monthly to address grievances before they become violence. You serve as secretary; Layla teaches at a joint school. Progress is slow—attacks still happen, old hatreds resurface—but children now play in streets once divided by invisible walls. Peace, fragile but real.

endings.title: Social Machinery Witness (Secret)
endings.text: You force the city to testify about itself. Checkpoint guards admit they enforced division for power. Clerics confess fear drove their rhetoric. Merchants reveal how economic competition became sectarian warfare. Your trial becomes an inquest into Sana'a's soul, and the verdict is collective responsibility. Families don't just reconcile—they transform. The social machinery that produced tragedy must now produce peace.
